Write $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=1}}}(G)$ for the Kirchhoff index based on the hubs-repelling resistance distance, $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}}_{\alpha=0}(G)$ for the standard Kirchhoff index, and $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=-1}}}(G)$ for the Kirchhoff index based on the hubs-attracting resistance distance.

**Kirchhoff-index ordering conjecture.** For $\alpha\in\{-1,1\}$,

$$
\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=1}}}(G)\geq\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}}_{\alpha=0}(G)\geq\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=-1}}}(G),
$$

with equality if and only if $G$ is regular.

The conjecture was formulated after computational experiments on more than 12,000 connected graphs with $5\leq n\leq 8$, and predicts that hubs-repelling navigation gives the largest Kirchhoff index while hubs-attracting navigation gives the smallest.     "statement": "Let ${\bf t}=t_0t_1t_2\cdots$ be the Thue–Morse sequence. For $j\geq 2$, define

$$
r_j(n):=\left|\{(x_1,\ldots,x_j):n=\sum_{1\leq i\leq j}x_i\text{ and }t_{x_i}=0\text{ for }1\leq i\leq j\}\right|
$$

and

$$
s_j(n):=\left|\{(x_1,\ldots,x_j):n=\sum_{1\leq i\leq j}x_i\text{ and }t_{x_i}=1\text{ for }1\leq i\leq j\}\right|.
$$

**Sixfold strict increase conjectures.** The sequences $r_6(n)$ and $s_6(n)$ satisfy

$$
r_6(n)<r_6(n+1)\qquad\text{for }n\geq 37,
$$

and

$$
s_6(n)<s_6(n+1)\qquad\text{for }n\geq 5.
$$

Numerical experiments suggest that both sequences are eventually strictly increasing; the conjectured thresholds are $37$ for $r_6$ and $5$ for $s_6$.",
